Once the data is here, a photo or scan that Pyxis reads itself is read on this computer, with no connection and no AI engine.

settings.crashWhy: Pyxis runs on your computer, so the person who makes it can't see the errors that happen to you: these reports are the only way to find and fix them. They don't slow Pyxis down, and a report goes only after an error.
settings.crashContents: A report holds the Pyxis and system versions, the error message and the place in the program where it started.
settings.crashNever: Pyxis doesn't add your files, chats or API keys, and it removes folder paths and quoted text from the error message, keeping only code names such as readFile. If Pyxis closes suddenly, though, the report includes part of its memory, which can hold fragments of what was on your screen.
settings.crashKept: Reports are deleted after 90 days, and you can take your consent back at any time in Settings, under Privacy.

planOverview.restoreHelp: Bring this exam back into your review queues and recommendations.
planOverview.archivedNotice: This exam is archived. It stays out of your review queues and recommendations.

install.title: Install
install.body: I run {{vendor}}'s official installer. It takes about a minute and needs no administrator password. This is the command:

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.body: Sign in with your {{account}} account. Your browser opens.
signIn.codeHint: If the browser shows a code, paste it here.
signIn.waitingTerminal: Waiting for you to sign in in the terminal…
signIn.terminalUnavailable: I couldn't open a terminal. Open one yourself, type this and press Enter:
signIn.waitingBrowser: Finish signing in in your browser. If no page opened, or you closed it, open it again below.

antigravity.open: Press the button below. A terminal window opens with Antigravity in it.
antigravity.choose: At "Select login method", choose Google OAuth with the arrow keys and press Enter.
antigravity.browser: Sign in with Google in your browser. If the page shows a code instead, paste it into the terminal and press Enter.
antigravity.back: Come back here. I notice the sign-in on my own, and then you can close the terminal.

books.title: Free PoliTost books
books.intro: Smartbooks written for PoliTost, free to use. The list comes from books.politost.it. Pyxis connects only while this window is open, or while the Sources page is open and holds one of these books, to check for a new version.
books.updateStarted: {{title}} is being updated to version {{version}}. Follow it in the background tasks.
books.updateInUse_one: {{count}} plan uses this book. Updating keeps the old text for that plan's citations, and marks lessons and quizzes that cite changed text as out of date. Then use Rebuild topics in the plan to pick up new chapters. Update it?
books.updateInUse_other: {{count}} plans use this book. Updating keeps the old text for those plans' citations, and marks lessons and quizzes that cite changed text as out of date. Then use Rebuild topics in each plan to pick up new chapters. Update it?

makeCards.title: Make flashcards
makeCards.noPlans: Flashcards belong to a topic of a plan. Create a plan first.
makeCards.hint: Pyxis writes short flashcards from this text. You check them before they are saved.
makeCards.failed: The flashcards could not be written. Check the selected engine, then try again.
makeCards.saveFailed: The flashcards could not be saved. Try again.
makeCards.cloze: Cloze: the words inside {{markup}} are hidden when you study.
makeCards.allDropped: You dropped every flashcard. Make again to get new ones.

oggi.title: Today
oggi.failed: Today's steps could not be loaded.
oggi.allDone: That's everything for today. Anything more is extra.

planner.title: Session plan
planner.intro: Pyxis spreads each exam's remaining work evenly over the days before it, within the hours you have. It plans again from what you actually did every time you open it, so a missed day moves to the days left.
planner.failed: The session plan could not be loaded.
planner.saveFailed: Your hours could not be saved. Try again.
planner.emptyBody: Give a plan an exam date in its settings, and the planner spreads its work over the weeks before the exam.
planner.weeklyHours: Hours you can study each week
planner.needed: To reach every target on time you need about {{hours}} h a week.
planner.setHours: Set your hours to see the plan per week and per day.
planner.behind_one: At this pace {{title}} reaches its {{target}}% target 1 day after the exam, and about {{atExam}}% by the exam.
planner.behind_other: At this pace {{title}} reaches its {{target}}% target {{count}} days after the exam, and about {{atExam}}% by the exam.
planner.behindNoTime: {{title}} has no study time before its exam, so it will not reach its {{target}}% target. Add hours to the weeks before it.
